summary: SSE choice index and final-token misalignment after proxy retry/rechunking
summary_detail: Customer reports that after multiple automatic reconnects through their corporate proxy, streaming SSE responses arrive with shifted choice indices and the final choice token sometimes missing, causing downstream JSON parsing errors in their message assembler.
description:
Issue summary: FableFinance sees intermittent deserialization errors and missing final tokens when resuming SSE streams across their corporate proxy. Impact: Customer production chat assistants sometimes return malformed choices which fail client-side parsing; affects ~8% of streamed responses during high concurrency windows. Environment: Customer is on enterprise Dedicated cluster in us-east behind an HTTP proxy that rewrites some headers and does buffering/chunking.

Observed behavior: After 2-3 quick reconnects (often during client-side network flapping), the resumed stream's 'choice' indices in final metadata no longer line up with the sequence of data events. In several captures the final token (closing bracket/terminator) is absent causing JSON parser failures. The customer is using SSE with resume-by-byte-offset logic on our API (resume_id + byte_offset).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer playback: Start SSE chat stream to endpoint /v1/chat/stream pinned to redwood-4b-chat. 2) Let server send initial chunks until partial choices visible. 3) Simulate network flapping: force two rapid reconnects by interrupting TCP connection, or have proxy reset/rewrite chunk boundaries. 4) Allow client to call resume with resume_id and byte_offset from last seen event. 5) Observe resumed stream: choice indices shift or final closing token missing and client JSON parse fails.
logs_and_evidence:
Attached excerpts from customer's stream capture (sanitized):
- event: message
  data: {"choices": [{"index":0,"text":"Hello"}]}
- event: message
  data: {"choices": [{"index":1,"text":"World"}]}
- (disconnect)
- client resume: POST /v1/streams/resume resume_id=abc123 offset=452
- resumed events:
  event: message
  data: {"choices": [{"index":0,"text":"Hello"}, {"index":1,"text":"World"}, {"index":2,"text":"!"}]}
- final metadata event shows choice_count=2 but three choices emitted.
Server-side logs: gateway shows proxy rechunking: upstream bytes=512 -> downstream chunks: 128, 198, 186. Proxy also adds a pseudo-event line 'retry: 2000' before the next data block.
Customer parsing error: JSONDecodeError at close: unexpected EOF (final ']' missing) in 3.4% of captured resumes.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: resume by byte-offset brittle in presence of in-path rechunking and proxy-inserted control lines. We reproduced similar misalignment by inserting a proxy that adds 'retry' pseudo-field lines and recombines TCP segments. Key observations: (a) Our resume uses byte offsets computed from raw bytes sent from server to gateway; when proxy re-writes/rechunks or inserts CRLF-only lines (e.g., 'retry: <ms>'), downstream byte mapping diverges and resume offset points to a different logical event boundary. (b) The client's assembler expects choice indices to be contiguous from 0..N-1; when proxy duplication of metadata or missing closing chunk happens the final 'end' event can be dropped. (c) WebSocket connections are not affected in the same way because they are framed end-to-end rather than being subject to SSE line-based reflow by proxies.
Repro on our side: Created a test harness that inserts 'retry: 1000' lines mid-stream and replays reconnections; this triggers the same misalignment. Traced resume logic to streaming-runtime/archive/resume_manager which currently stores resume offsets as absolute bytes in the SSE payload.
root_cause: Resume-by-byte-offset for SSE is fragile in real-world networks where intermediaries (corporate proxies, CDNs) may re-chunk or inject control lines. The injected 'retry' line and different chunk boundaries lead to offset mismatches so the resumed stream can duplicate or omit event framing, causing choice index mismatches and occasional missing terminator tokens.
mitigation_and_workaround:
Immediate customer workaround provided: 1) Switch to WebSocket streaming (ws) for critical sessions — avoids intermediate re-chunking and preserves frame boundaries. 2) If SSE required, ask proxy team to disable response buffering and any SSE rewriting (disable 'retry' injection) for the customer origin. 3) Client-side: add a tolerant parser that can recover from duplicated or out-of-order choice indices by renormalizing choices based on seen 'id' or dropping duplicate indices. We supplied a small JS snippet to normalize choices.
Support actioned: sent proxy configuration guidance and shared WebSocket migration checklist. Customer applied websocket migration and saw errors drop to ~0.2%.
resolution_plan:
Short-term (1 week): Add defensive server-side resume mapping: include a monotonically increasing 'event_seq' field in each SSE 'message' event and make resume API accept resume_seq in addition to byte_offset. This lets resume align to event boundaries even if byte offsets change. Implement feature flag and backward compatibility for existing clients.
Medium-term (1 month): Update streaming-runtime to emit sequence numbers and update resume_manager to prefer sequence-based resume, falling back to byte offsets. Add automated tests simulating proxy re-chunking.
Long-term: Add documentation and SDK helpers for SSE vs WS tradeoffs and recommend websocket for enterprise behind known proxies.
